name: Atlas Trend KR
description: Time-series momentum across a fixed basket of Korea-listed ETFs, in won. Holds only what is trending in its own price, sizes what it holds by realised volatility, and parks in CD-rate funds when nothing is. One monthly rebalance, or nothing.

managers.name: Atlas Trend KR
managers.description: Scores five roles of Korea-listed ETF on an ensemble of 1, 3, 6 and 12-month won-denominated returns, holds only the positive ones at inverse-volatility weights under a portfolio volatility target, and puts everything else in a CD-rate fund. Hedged and unhedged share classes compete for the same role and are never held together. Returns one REBALANCE carrying the whole basket, or WAIT.

capabilities.reason: Two vendors with two jobs. 토스증권 supplies the adjusted won price history the trend is measured on; 금융위원회's 증권상품시세정보 supplies the NAV, the underlying index and the fund size that say whether the fund is worth holding at all. Both answers are the vendor's, unread by Aumos.
The proposal is a set of weights for the whole book, so the book as it stands is the only thing that says whether those weights are already held. Without it every run would propose a trade.
Whether this book is currently in the all-cash state, and since when. A trend system's behaviour depends on where it already is, and that is a fact about the book rather than about any one asset.
To record entering or leaving that state, once, when it changes — so the next run and the other managers on this book can read it instead of inferring it from weights.
